workflow_hypothesis: Truncated mapped backing store causes fatal later access
pattern: Live memory-mapped persistent storage can be externally truncated before a later update accesses the mapping.
description: A persistent store remains open while its backing file is externally shortened, and a subsequent operation accesses mapped data using the original layout.
precondition: A persistent file-backed store has live memory-mapped contents and assumes the backing file remains sufficiently sized and structurally valid.
critical_operation: A later update or lookup dereferences mapped storage based on the previously valid file layout.
interference: An external actor truncates or otherwise shortens the backing file while the store remains open.
invalid_assumption: The existing mapping still refers to valid backing storage covering the original addresses and layout.
failure: The access produces a fatal storage-library error or process-terminating memory fault instead of a recoverable error.
search_strategy: Check whether live mappings can outlast validation of the backing file's current size.
Check update and lookup paths for mapped-memory dereferences without backing-file length validation.
Check whether external truncation or shrinkage is handled before accessing mapped data.
Check whether invalidated mappings become recoverable errors rather than fatal faults.

evidence.supports: The report reproduces an open persistent store whose backing file is emptied externally, after which a write reaches invalid mapped storage and terminates the process; disabling mapping avoids the reproduced crash in the described configuration.

scope_note: Singleton cluster: scoped to persistent stores using live memory mappings where the backing file may be truncated or shortened externally. The report does not establish a rule for ordinary buffered I/O, file replacement without shrinkage, or every form of mapping invalidation.
